decisions.detail: QUOTE: "Before the network call, the post is written locally with a `pending_post_id` and a temporary id, so it shows in the UI immediately." and "Any other error: the post is saved with `props.failed = true`" | WHY: The answer states the post is written locally before the send and is kept and marked `failed = true` on non-removal errors. || QUOTE: "Before the network call, the post is written locally with a `pending_post_id` and a temporary id" and "the post is saved with `props.failed = true`" | WHY: The answer states the post is saved locally before the send and is kept and flagged `failed = true` on error. || QUOTE: Before the network call, the post is written locally with a `pending_post_id` and a temporary id, so it shows in the UI immediately. ... the post is saved with `props.failed = true` and `update_at` set to now. | WHY: The answer states the post is written locally before sending and, on failure, is kept in the local database with `props.failed = true`.

decisions.mark: states that a retry happens only when the user chooses "Try Again" on the failed post, and calls `retryFailedPost`
decisions.detail: QUOTE: It is wired to the "Try Again" item (`post.failed.retry`) in the failed-post bottom sheet (`app/components/post_list/post/body/failed/index.tsx:46-49`). | WHY: The answer says the send is never retried automatically, that "Try Again" is the user action in the failed-post sheet, and that it calls `retryFailedPost`. || QUOTE: It is wired to the "Try Again" item (`post.failed.retry`) in the failed-post bottom sheet (`app/components/post_list/post/body/failed/index.tsx:46-49`). | WHY: The answer says the send is never retried automatically and that "Try Again" in the failed-post sheet triggers `retryFailedPost`, which covers both parts of the item.

decisions.mark: concludes that `retryFailedPost` makes exactly one new attempt with no loop or backoff, and on failure marks the post failed again (or removes it for the same three errors)
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "It rebuilds the API payload from the stored model with `toApi()` and calls `client.createPost` again. Unlike the first attempt, this call does not set `noRetry`, so the network layer's default retry policy applies. I did not verify that default." | WHY: The answer says a retry attempt is made and that on failure the post is marked failed again, but it never concludes there is exactly one attempt with no loop or backoff. It instead suggests the network layer's default retry policy may apply, which contradicts the item. || QUOTE: "It rebuilds the API payload from the stored model with `toApi()` and calls `client.createPost` again... On failure, it marks the post failed again. The same three removal cases apply, so a deleted root or read-only Town Square removes the post instead." | WHY: The answer says retry marks failed again or removes it, but it doesn't conclude there is exactly one attempt with no loop or backoff. It says the default network retry policy might apply and that it didn't check this, which undercuts the "no loop or backoff" claim.

decisions.mark: notes that `createPost` reports a failed send as success to its caller (`{data: true}`), so the failure is visible only in the stored post
decisions.detail: QUOTE: "The function returns `{data: true}`, not an error. The caller is not told the send failed." | WHY: The answer states that `createPost` returns `{data: true}` even when the send failed, and that the failure is stored on the post as `props.failed = true`. || QUOTE: "The function returns `{data: true}`, not an error.
